newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PEAC to expand Manila-Seoul cargo capacity.
newsitem.headline: PEAC to expand Manila-Seoul cargo capacity.

text.p: Philippine cargo airline Pacific East Asia Cargo Airlines (PEAC) says it plans to offer more capacity on flights to Korea.
PEAC currently operates a British Aerospace 146 freighter from Manila to Seoul.
Airline managing director Benjamin Solis told Reuters that he will be upgrading to a Boeing 727 in the near future.

The airline is the Philippines designated carrier to Korea and was granted more rights when a confidential memorandum of understanding (CMU) was signed between the Philippine and Korean governments last November, he added.

A recent bid by large rival Philippine Airlines to also fly a freighter service from Manila to Seoul failed when the flag carrier's petition to the Civil Aeronautics Board of the Philippines was rejected, Solis said.
Philippine Airlines says it now has plans to offer belly cargo capacity from Cebu to Seoul using one of its Airbus Industrie A330 aircraft due to arrive as part of its fleet modernisation programme.
PEAC, in TNT Asia has a minority stake, says it also has plans to increase its fleet by two leased aircraft per year starting from next year.
The all- cargo carrier operates to six destinations inluding Hong Kong says it plans to activate two unused routes to Bangkok and Kuala Lumpur in about two years time.
Solis said a priority is to start flying into China but negotiations on rights are at a standstill.

"We met with a Chinese delegation three months ago which said PEAC can fly into China, but they cited non-aviation issues such as tax problems Chinese carriers are having with the Philippines that need need to be settled first." he added.
"It's a stalemate situation with China," Solis said. - Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+44 171 542 5017
